title: RESEARCH: oracle comparison harness and match-rate metrics
description: Design how correctness is measured, before building the things being measured. The pbpstats oracle gives possession level start types and times for the same season, so comparison can be exact rather than statistical. Decide what to compare: possession counts per game, boundary times, start type strings, and lineup composition. Decide how to report: a per-game match rate with an investigable failure list, not a single aggregate number that hides which games are broken. Also design the independent checks that do not depend on the oracle - per player stint minutes reconciled against official box score minutes, structural invariants such as possessions tiling each period with no gaps or overlaps, and sanity aggregates such as league average points per possession landing in the expected 1.10 to 1.20 band. That last one matters because it catches segmentation bugs the oracle comparison can miss. NOTE this harness is reused later as the Rust port contract in E10, so design it to compare two implementations, not just one against the oracle.
acceptance_criteria: A defined comparison methodology with a target match rate threshold and a documented rationale for that threshold. Failure reporting localizes to specific game, period and event. Independent non-oracle checks specified. Harness design supports implementation-versus-implementation comparison for the later Rust port. Findings written to docs/research/ as a committed document. Target schema revised if the research warrants it. Implementation issues filed under this epic with dependencies set. This issue is NOT closed by writing code - it is closed by producing the findings and the issue breakdown.
notes:
NOTE from hoops-1lg.2.3 (2026-09-11): reusable report primitives now exist at hoopstate/ingest/reports.py — join_report() (rows, matched, unmatched, match rate, bounded unmatched-key sample, duplicate right-side key count) and key_coverage() (per-group distinct-value stats plus reference keys with no rows), both returning frozen dataclasses rather than printing, with a named-report registry and a python -m CLI.

Build the oracle comparison harness on these rather than reinventing match-rate reporting. They already satisfy this issue's 'failure reporting localizes to specific game, period and event' requirement in shape (bounded failure lists, not a single aggregate) and are implementation-agnostic, so they carry over to the E10 implementation-versus-implementation comparison.

title: RESEARCH: possession segmentation edge cases and vocabulary
description: Settle the segmentation rules against real games rather than from first principles. Baseline rules: a possession ENDS on a made field goal, a made final free throw of a trip, a defensive rebound live or team, a turnover, or end of period. A possession does NOT end on an offensive rebound, which instead opens a new chance within the same possession, nor on and-one free throws following a made basket, nor on technical or flagrant free throws, timeouts, substitutions or kicked ball violations. Two known miscount sources need explicit handling: TEAM REBOUNDS, where a miss deflected out of bounds off the defense is logged as a team rebound but the offense retains possession; and OFFENSIVE REBOUNDS splitting a possession into chances, where modelling possession and chance as separate tables is what keeps points-per-possession and points-per-chance both correct - collapsing them makes one of the two wrong. Also settle the start and end type vocabulary, aligning to the pbpstats naming such as OffAtRimMiss, OffLiveBallTurnover, OffMadeFG and OffDeadBall, so that oracle comparison in E7 is a direct string equality test rather than a mapping exercise.
acceptance_criteria: An enumerated rule set with a real example game and event for each rule and each edge case. A decided possession/chance table split. A start and end type vocabulary aligned to pbpstats naming, with any deliberate divergence documented and justified. Findings written to docs/research/ as a committed document. Target schema revised if the research warrants it. Implementation issues filed under this epic with dependencies set. This issue is NOT closed by writing code - it is closed by producing the findings and the issue breakdown.

title: RESEARCH: period starter resolution strategy
description: The central hard problem of the project. Walking substitutions forward handles the easy 90 percent. The failure mode is that a player who is on court at period start, records no event all period, and is never substituted is COMPLETELY INVISIBLE in the play-by-play. The common heuristic - a player whose first period event is being subbed out must have started - misses these and silently yields four-player lineups that poison every downstream aggregate. Evaluate three resolutions on the full 2023-24 season and MEASURE how many periods each leaves unresolved, rather than picking on intuition. ONE: matchups data from 2017 onward, a direct observation of who was on court, cheapest if coverage is good. TWO: boxscoretraditionalv2 with RangeType 2 and a one-second StartRange/EndRange at period start, which returns exactly the players on court in that window - definitive, but one API call per unresolved period against a rate-limited endpoint. THREE: a committed manual override file keyed by game id and period; the reference implementation ships one for exactly this reason, so expect a handful of games per season to need it regardless. Likely the answer is a cascade of all three.
acceptance_criteria: Each strategy measured on 2023-24 with a count of periods left unresolved and the API cost where applicable. A chosen cascade with its rationale. Confirmation that the exactly-five-per-team invariant can be asserted as a hard failure across all 1230 games under the chosen approach. Findings written to docs/research/ as a committed document. Target schema revised if the research warrants it. Implementation issues filed under this epic with dependencies set. This issue is NOT closed by writing code - it is closed by producing the findings and the issue breakdown.
notes:
AMENDMENT from hoops-1lg.2.3 (2026-09-11), measured on real matchups_2023 data:

Option ONE is weaker than this issue assumes. The matchups dataset has NO period column. matchups_2023.csv is 48 columns, one row per (offensive player, defensive player) pair PER GAME, carrying total matchup_minutes, matchup_minutes_sort, partial_possessions and a matchup box-score line. It is a game-level aggregate, not a per-possession or per-period observation, so it CANNOT directly answer 'who was on the floor at the start of period 3'.

What it can still do: bound the per-game candidate set, and rank players by partial_possessions / matchup_minutes as a likelihood prior for the invisible-starter case.

Measured 2023 coverage: 1227 of nbastats' 1230 games have matchups rows (3 games have none at all). Distinct players per game mean 21.46, median 21, min 16, max 30, versus mean 24.95 distinct PLAYER1_ID per game in nbastats.

Consequence: options TWO (boxscoretraditionalv2 RangeType 2 range query) and THREE (committed manual override file) carry correspondingly more weight in the cascade. Budget the research accordingly.

Re-measure for any season with: python -m hoopstate.ingest.reports matchups_game_coverage --season <year>

title: RESEARCH: event taxonomy, ordering pathologies, clock normalization
description: Three linked questions that must be answered before any canonical event table is written. FIRST, event taxonomy: map stats.nba.com EVENTMSGTYPE and EVENTMSGACTIONTYPE onto a semantic enum, and reconcile it with the data.nba.com vocabulary. This taxonomy becomes the Rust sum type later, so getting the categories right has long reach. SECOND, ordering pathologies: stats.nba.com PBP contains genuinely out-of-order events - rebounds logged before the shot they rebound, scrambled free throw sequences, substitutions ambiguous against same-timestamp made shots. Catalogue the actual cases present in 2023-24 with counts and example game ids, rather than assuming the known list is complete. datanba carries an explicit offense team id on every event and is the cross-check. THIRD, clock normalization: PCTIMESTRING to clock_seconds and to absolute elapsed_seconds, handling overtime periods correctly. Possession segmentation in E5 cannot be correct until ordering is fixed, so this is genuinely upstream.
acceptance_criteria: A documented event taxonomy with every observed EVENTMSGTYPE/ACTIONTYPE pair accounted for and none silently falling through. A catalogue of ordering pathologies with frequency counts across the season and reproducible example games. A clock normalization rule covering regulation and overtime. Findings written to docs/research/ as a committed document. Target schema revised if the research warrants it. Implementation issues filed under this epic with dependencies set. This issue is NOT closed by writing code - it is closed by producing the findings and the issue breakdown.

title: Oracle ingest with enforced quarantine
description: The pbpstats_2023 dataset contains possession level data with start types and times, derived by the reference implementation. This is the validation oracle and, later, the Rust port contract. It must never feed the core model, only the test suite. Ingest it into a separate oracle zone and enforce the boundary mechanically rather than by convention.
acceptance_criteria: pbpstats_2023 lands in the oracle zone. An automated guard fails if any module outside validate/ or tests/ imports or reads oracle data. The guard is part of the default test run.

title: Bronze conversion: shotdetail and matchups
description:
shotdetail carries shot x/y coordinates and zones, joining to events on GAME_ID plus GAME_EVENT_ID. matchups, available from 2017 onward, lists offensive and defensive matchup pairs.

CORRECTION (measured during planning, 2026-09-11): matchups is a GAME-LEVEL aggregate of matchup pairs, not a per-possession record. matchups_2023.csv has 48 columns and NO period column — each row is one (offensive player, defensive player) pair for one game, carrying total matchup_minutes, partial_possessions and a matchup box-score line. It is therefore a game-level roster and weighting seed for E4, NOT a direct period-level on-court observation. See hoops-1lg.4.1, whose option ONE was written on the wrong premise.

Verification is delivered as re-runnable code (hoopstate/ingest/reports.py), not as prose in a docstring, so join rates and coverage can be re-measured for any season and reused by E4 and E7.
acceptance_criteria: shotdetail_2023 and matchups_2023 land as typed parquet in bronze, season partitioned, with explicit dtypes (never inferred). The shotdetail event join key is verified to join cleanly against nbastats, including a count of duplicate right-side keys (join fan-out risk). Matchups player-id coverage is quantified PER GAME — per period is not possible, the column does not exist. Verification ships as a re-runnable report module with a CLI, offline-tested, whose named reports reproduce the measured 2023 figures. Downstream specs (hoops-1lg.4.1, hoops-1lg.7.1) updated with the matchups correction and the availability of the report primitives.
notes:
MEASURED 2023 (real data, via the new report CLI):

shotdetail_event_join — shotdetail_2023 (GAME_ID, GAME_EVENT_ID) -> nbastats_2023 (GAME_ID, EVENTNUM)
  left rows 218701; matched 218698 (99.998628%); unmatched 3; duplicate rhs keys 3
  unmatched sample [('22300770', 635), ('22300091', 351), ('22300163', 655)]

matchups_game_coverage — matchups_2023, distinct players per game
  1227 of 1230 games; 3 missing; min/max 16/30; mean/median 21.46/21
  missing games ['22301192', '22301230', '22300383']

datanba_game_coverage — datanba_2023, distinct players per game (the hoops-1lg.2.2 prose retrofit)
  1228 of 1230 games; 2 missing; min/max 19/32; mean/median 24.08/23
  missing games ['22301195', '22301177']

Row counts: shotdetail_2023 218701, matchups_2023 230703.
The 3 duplicate (GAME_ID, EVENTNUM) keys are a real fan-out risk in nbastats and are why JoinReport reports duplicates separately from match rate — a duplicated key matches perfectly and still corrupts downstream aggregates.

Re-measure at any time: python -m hoopstate.ingest.reports --all --season YYYY
close_reason: Implemented: shotdetail (24 cols) and matchups (48 cols) bronze schemas, shared bronze_parquet_path, new re-runnable hoopstate/ingest/reports.py with join/coverage primitives, three named reports and a CLI. 34 offline tests; make check clean; all measured 2023 figures reproduced end-to-end.

title: Manifest driven bulk loader, streaming tar.xz to parquet
description: Ingest from the shufinskiy/nba_data archive, which publishes pre-scraped tar.xz wrapped CSVs. The manifest at raw.githubusercontent.com/shufinskiy/nba_data/main/list_data.txt is 514 lines of name=url pairs, confirmed live. Naming is data_season for regular season and data_po_season for playoffs, where season is the starting year. Stream decompress straight into parquet without persisting extracted CSV, which avoids a roughly 300 MB per season transient spike on a boot disk that cannot afford it. Checksum and cache downloads in the cold zone so a completed season is never re-fetched.
acceptance_criteria: Loader parses the manifest, downloads a named dataset, verifies checksum, and writes parquet without an intermediate CSV on disk. Re-running is a no-op for already ingested data. Raw archives land in the cold NAS zone. Failure mid-download leaves no partial parquet.

title: Bronze conversion: nbastats and datanba play-by-play
description: Convert both play-by-play sources to typed parquet, one to one with source, partitioned by season. Both matter and for different reasons: nbastats is the primary event feed, while datanba carries an explicit offense team id on every event, which is the cross-check that catches the out-of-order events stats.nba.com is known to contain. Document the schema of each.
acceptance_criteria: nbastats_2023 and datanba_2023 land as typed parquet in bronze. Column types explicit, not inferred. Schema documented. Row counts match source CSV.

title: Portable storage profile resolution
description:
Resolve all data paths through a storage PROFILE rather than assuming one machine. Three profiles must work, and the default must be the portable one so a fresh checkout in a sandbox runs with zero configuration.

PROFILE ephemeral (default; cloud sessions and CI): every zone under one scratch directory on local disk. Nothing is assumed to persist between sessions, so raw archives are re-fetched on demand and the download cache is keyed so a repeat run inside one session is cheap. A cloud VM has 30 GB, 16 GB RAM and 4 vCPU, which is ample for a full season end to end, so this profile has no split and no preflight.

PROFILE local: the hot/cold split for the development machine, where local disk is at 98 percent with about 4 GiB free and the NAS at /Volumes/home has 3.4 TiB. Cold zones on NAS for raw archives and non-active-season bronze; hot zones local for silver, gold, oracle, active season bronze, and the DuckDB file. The DuckDB file MUST stay local under any profile because DuckDB does not support database files on network filesystems and SMB locking is unreliable enough to risk corruption.

Selected by HOOPSTATE_PROFILE, with individual zones overridable by HOOPSTATE_HOT and HOOPSTATE_COLD. The point of the split is that NOTHING downstream of this issue should know which profile is active - ingestion, the model, and the tests all ask for a zone path and get one. NAS specific preflight is deliberately NOT in this issue; it lives in its own local-only issue so that ingestion is never gated on hardware a cloud session cannot reach.
acceptance_criteria: HOOPSTATE_PROFILE selects between ephemeral and local; ephemeral is the default. HOOPSTATE_HOT and HOOPSTATE_COLD override individual zones. A fresh checkout with no environment variables set resolves every zone and runs the test suite - verified in CI, which is the standing proof the portable path works. The DuckDB path is asserted to be on local disk under every profile. No module outside this one branches on which profile is active.

title: Relocate toolchain caches to NAS and cap build artifact size
description: The toolchains, not the data, are the storage problem: one season of data is 39.6 MB compressed and all 30 seasons are about 1.2 GB, while a Rust target dir with arrow/polars/duckdb deps routinely reaches 3-5 GB, rustup about 1.5 GB, a Python venv 1-1.5 GB and the uv cache about 1 GB. That is 6-9 GB against 5.7 GB free. Move read-mostly caches to NAS and cap what stays local. Note that uv hardlinks from cache into venv and hardlinks cannot cross filesystems, so a NAS uv cache silently falls back to copying: slower installs and no saving inside the venv. Evaluate whether pruning locally is the better trade.
acceptance_criteria: RUSTUP_HOME and CARGO_HOME point at NAS. Decision recorded on UV_CACHE_DIR placement with its rationale. Cargo profile sets debug to 0 or line-tables-only, which typically cuts target size 50-70 percent and is the single biggest win available. Documented local footprint budget with a check that reports current usage.
notes: LOCAL ONLY. A cloud session has 30 GB of disk and a fresh VM each time, so there is nothing to relocate and no cache to preserve. This issue exists purely for the development machine.

title: Scaffold polyglot workspace on Python 3.14
description: Create the python/ and rust/ workspace layout from day one so the later Rust port is an addition rather than a restructuring. Set up flox with python314 and uv, src layout under python/src/nbaviz with ingest, model, derive, validate and db packages. Pin dependencies: polars, duckdb, pyarrow, pandas, plus pytest and ruff. IMPORTANT: polars publishes a pure-Python shim that depends on polars-runtime-32, which ships cp310-abi3 wheels. abi3 is forward compatible with CPython 3.10 and up, so polars works on 3.14 even though its classifiers only list up to 3.13. This is untested by the vendor, so verify it.
acceptance_criteria: Workspace created with python/ and rust/ top level dirs. flox activate gives Python 3.14. uv sync resolves all deps. A polars smoke test imports polars, builds a DataFrame, runs a group_by and a shift/over expression, and writes plus reads parquet, all passing on 3.14. If polars fails, fall back to python313 3.13.15 and record the reason in the issue notes.
close_reason: Polyglot workspace scaffolded; polars verified working on CPython 3.14.7 via cp310-abi3; smoke test in default run; finding recorded in docs/research/0001.

title: E7 Validation and data quality
description: Prove the derived model is correct. Oracle comparison harness against pbpstats, box score minute reconciliation for lineups, structural invariant checks, and golden game regression fixtures covering known pathologies.

title: E5 Possession and chance model
description: Segment the event stream into possessions, and split possessions into chances at offensive rebounds. Encode possession end rules, handle team rebounds and and-one free throws, and classify start and end types using a pbpstats compatible vocabulary.

title: E3 Canonical event model
description: Unify stats.nba.com and data.nba.com play-by-play into one canonical typed event stream: semantic event taxonomy, clock normalization to absolute elapsed seconds, corrected event ordering, and offense/defense team attribution.

title: E4 Lineup reconstruction
description: Reconstruct which five players are on court for each team at every event. The hard part is period starter inference: a player who starts a period, records no event, and is never substituted is invisible in the PBP. Must assert the exactly-five-per-team invariant as a hard failure.

title: E2 Ingestion
description: Bulk ingest from the shufinskiy/nba_data archive rather than scraping stats.nba.com, which is Cloudflare rate limited and blocks most cloud IPs. Manifest driven loader streaming tar.xz straight to parquet, bronze conversion for each source dataset, and quarantined ingest of the pbpstats validation oracle.

title: E1 Foundation
description: Project scaffolding: polyglot Python/Rust workspace, flox and uv environment on Python 3.14, hot/cold storage configuration split between local disk and NAS, toolchain cache relocation, DuckDB conventions, and the lint/test/CI harness. Everything downstream depends on this.

title: Rich NBA play-by-play data model
description: Derive a richer model from public NBA play-by-play data than the raw feed provides. Raw PBP has two structural gaps: it logs substitutions but never states who is on the court, and it is a flat event list with no possession or sequence structure. This epic covers reconstructing on-court lineups, segmenting possessions and chances, and deriving event-context features, validated against pbpstats as an independent oracle. Scope is one season end-to-end first (2023-24), then breadth. Plan: ~/.claude/plans/i-want-to-design-tender-hollerith.md

title: CoverageReport: name the extreme groups, and render reports as tables
description:
Two related gaps in hoopstate/ingest/reports.py output, found while reading real 2023 results.

1. CoverageReport reports min/max per-group counts but not WHICH group. missing_sample names the groups with no rows, so a missing game is directly actionable, but an outlier game is not — identifying that matchups' 16-player game is 22301185 currently requires querying the parquet by hand. Add minimum_key/maximum_key.

2. format() emits a loose label/value list with bare labels like 'min / max', which does not say what is being counted. Render both report types as an aligned table with labels built from the report's own unit/measure, e.g. 'fewest distinct players in a game' rather than 'min'.
acceptance_criteria: CoverageReport carries minimum_key and maximum_key (None when the frame is empty), populated by key_coverage. Both JoinReport.format() and CoverageReport.format() render an aligned table. Coverage labels name the unit and measure explicitly rather than using bare min/max/mean. Extreme groups are shown alongside their counts. Offline tests cover the new fields, the empty-frame case, and the rendered labels. make check clean.
close_reason: CoverageReport now names the extreme groups (minimum_key/maximum_key) and both report types render as aligned tables with labels that spell out unit and measure. Evidence samples sorted for diffable re-runs. 5 new tests; make check clean; verified against real 2023 data.

title: Report: datanba oftid vs nbastats event ordering cross-check
description:
hoops-1lg.2.2's bronze.py docstring claims datanba's explicit offense-team id (oftid) is 'an independent observation of who had the ball, a cross-check that catches the out-of-order events stats.nba.com is known to contain'. The game-overlap half of 2.2's prose was retrofitted into reports.py as datanba_game_coverage in hoops-1lg.2.3; this claim was not, and remains an unmeasured assertion.

Add a named report to hoopstate/ingest/reports.py that measures it: align datanba events to nbastats events within a game, and quantify how often the offense-team id implied by nbastats event ordering disagrees with datanba's oftid. The disagreement rate is the number that tells E3 whether oftid is a usable ordering oracle or just corroboration.
acceptance_criteria: A named report (e.g. datanba_possession_agreement) is registered in REPORTS and runnable from the CLI. It is built on the existing join_report/key_coverage primitives rather than new bespoke reporting code. It is offline-tested against synthetic bronze parquet. The measured 2023 disagreement rate is recorded on this issue, and bronze.py's docstring points at the report instead of asserting the claim in prose.

title: NAS mount preflight and device-id verification
description:
LOCAL ONLY. Not reachable from a cloud session and must never gate work that is.

The local profile writes cold zones to an SMB mount. CRITICAL HAZARD: when that mount drops from sleep or a network blip, macOS lets a process create a regular directory at the mountpoint, so writes silently land on a boot disk that has roughly 4 GiB free. Preflight must compare device ids via stat -f rather than merely testing that the path exists, and must fail loudly instead of silently filling the boot disk.

Also covers atomic write discipline for the cold zone: parquet writes go to a temp name then atomic-rename, so an interrupted write over a flaky network mount never leaves a readable-but-truncated file.
acceptance_criteria: Preflight verifies cold paths are genuinely mounted by device-id comparison and raises a clear error when not. A test simulates an absent mountpoint and asserts the failure is loud, not silent. Parquet writes use temp name plus atomic rename. Skipped cleanly and without error under the ephemeral profile.

title: Golden game fixture selection and committed test parquet
description: Choose a small set of games that between them exercise every pathological path, and commit them as small parquet fixtures so the test suite runs fast and offline with no NAS dependency. Target coverage: a double overtime game, a game with an ejection, a game with a flagrant foul and its free throws, a game with a coach challenge and an overturned call, a game requiring a manual period starter override from the E4 cascade, a game with a high offensive rebound count to exercise the chance split, and an ordinary blowout as the boring control. Record WHY each game was chosen alongside the fixture, because a fixture whose purpose is undocumented gets deleted by a future maintainer who cannot tell what it protects.
acceptance_criteria: Fixture games chosen with a documented reason for each. Committed as parquet under tests/fixtures at a size appropriate for version control. The test suite runs against fixtures with no NAS mount and no network access.

title: Reference dimensions: teams, players, games, seasons
description: The small slowly-changing dimension tables every other table joins against. Team identity is the fiddly part - franchise relocations and renames mean a team id is stable but its name and abbreviation are not, so the dimension needs to be season scoped rather than a single current-name lookup. Game dimension carries date, season, season type (regular, playoff, play-in), home and away team ids, and the arena, which later supports rest-days and travel covariates in E6. Player dimension is derived from the ids appearing in play-by-play plus box scores. This is independent of the taxonomy spike and can proceed in parallel with it.
acceptance_criteria: Team, player, game and season dimensions materialized as silver parquet. Team names are season scoped so a relocated franchise resolves correctly for a historical season. Every team id, player id and game id appearing in bronze play-by-play resolves against a dimension row, verified as a test rather than assumed.

title: RESEARCH: work backwards from flagship visuals to schema requirements
description: Runs EARLY and deliberately, despite visualization being a deferred deliverable. The reason is concrete: the flagship visuals - a game flow river showing score margin over time banded by lineup with leverage overlaid, a substitution gantt chart, a player-pair chemistry network, a Markov or Sankey transition diagram, and context-conditioned shot charts - all require possession level score state, lineup bands, and a leverage value attached to each possession. Those are cheap to include in the silver schema now and expensive to retrofit once marts are built on top of it. This spike builds NO UI. Its only job is to work backwards from the target visuals to the columns and grain the schema must carry, and to feed those requirements into E3 and E5 before they are implemented.
acceptance_criteria: Each flagship visual decomposed into the data grain and columns it requires. A concrete list of schema additions or changes handed to E3 and E5, filed as issues or comments against them. Explicitly no UI code written. Findings written to docs/research/ as a committed document. Target schema revised if the research warrants it. Implementation issues filed under this epic with dependencies set. This issue is NOT closed by writing code - it is closed by producing the findings and the issue breakdown.

title: RESEARCH: derivable context features without tracking data
description: Determine what event context can honestly be derived from play-by-play alone, and what cannot. Candidates: previous and next event type, seconds since previous event, transition versus half court classification from possession start type plus duration, estimated shot clock derived from chance start, seconds since timeout, and rest/fatigue covariates computed from lineup stints. The fatigue covariates are the distinctive ones - consecutive seconds on court per player, and rest differential between the two fives on the floor - and they are only possible because E4 produces stint data. Be explicit about which features are estimates rather than observations, since shot clock in particular is inferred and will carry error that downstream analysis must not treat as ground truth.
acceptance_criteria: A feature list with a derivation rule for each, and an explicit confidence or error characterization for every estimated feature. Features that cannot be derived without tracking data are named and ruled out rather than left ambiguous. Findings written to docs/research/ as a committed document. Target schema revised if the research warrants it. Implementation issues filed under this epic with dependencies set. This issue is NOT closed by writing code - it is closed by producing the findings and the issue breakdown.

title: Lint, test and CI harness
description: ruff for lint and format, pytest for tests, with a make or task entrypoint. Include the storage preflight and polars smoke test in the default test run so environment breakage surfaces immediately rather than mid pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: ruff check and ruff format pass clean. pytest runs and collects. A single command runs lint plus tests. CI config present even if only run locally for now.
close_reason: ruff lint+format clean, pytest green, make check runs both, .github/workflows/ci.yml runs them on every push and PR. Storage preflight joins the default test run when hoops-1lg.1.2 lands.

title: DuckDB conventions and rebuild helper
description: Parquet on disk is the source of truth; the DuckDB file holds views over parquet plus materialized gold marts, so it must always be safe to delete and rebuild. Establish naming conventions, view definitions per zone, and a single command that rebuilds the database from parquet.
acceptance_criteria: A documented convention for views over each zone. One command rebuilds nbaviz.duckdb from parquet with no data loss. Deleting the DuckDB file and rebuilding produces identical query results.

title: E9 Visualization foundations
description: Deliberately early, despite viz being deferred. Work backwards from flagship target visuals to the schema requirements they imply, so possession level score state, lineup bands, and leverage are present in silver from the start rather than retrofitted. Builds no UI.

title: E6 Context and sequence features
description: Derive the event adjacency and context features that motivated the project: previous and next event type, inter event timing, transition classification, estimated shot clock, and rest/fatigue covariates.

title: Build the read-only axum API over gold marts
description: The final port step: async, extractors, serialization. Last by design and only once the gold marts are stable, because a service built over a moving schema is rework. It stays a thin read only layer over DuckDB with no business logic, which is exactly why the pipeline language never constrained it. Depends on the gold/v1 contract from E11 being pinned.
acceptance_criteria: A read only axum service over gold marts with no business logic in the handler layer. Responses conform to the pinned gold/v1 schema. The schema snapshot test from E11 covers the endpoints.

title: Port ingestion to Rust
description: Uses the arrow, parquet and polars crates plus real error handling and some async. More plumbing than concept, and polars being first class in Rust means expression code maps closely to the Python side. Confirm the target directory size against the local disk budget from E1 while doing this, since these dependencies are the largest single consumer of local disk.
acceptance_criteria: Rust ingestion produces parquet byte identical to the Python loader for at least one season. Build artifact size measured and within the E1 budget with debug symbols disabled.

title: Port lineup reconstruction to Rust
description: The first step needing real state management - HashMap and ownership across a full game walk. The payoff is that the five player invariant becomes a type, Lineup([PlayerId; 5]), enforced at construction rather than asserted at runtime. Gated on the Python lineup model reconciling against box score minutes.
acceptance_criteria: Rust lineup and stint output byte identical to Python across the full season. The five player invariant is enforced by the type rather than a runtime assert.
notes: REAL GATE: the Python lineup model must reconcile against box-score minutes before this starts. The dependency on the E4 research spike is a proxy; repoint it at the implementation issue that spike files.

title: Port event taxonomy to Rust sum types
description: The first Rust step, chosen for teaching value. The taxonomy from the E3 spike becomes an enum with exhaustive match. This is pure sum types - no lifetimes, no async, no borrow checker fights - and it is simultaneously the highest value type safety win in the whole port: an unhandled event subtype becomes a compile error rather than a silent None that corrupts a season of derived data.
acceptance_criteria: Every event type and subtype from the Python taxonomy represented as a Rust enum. Parsing from bronze is exhaustive with no catch-all arm that silently swallows unknowns. Round trip parse and serialize tested against the Python taxonomy output.
notes: REAL GATE: the taxonomy from the E3 spike must be settled before this starts. Dependency on the spike is the proxy; repoint at the concrete taxonomy implementation issue once filed.

title: Port possession segmentation to Rust
description: A state machine over owned data, introducing modelling state transitions in the type system while staying self contained. Gated on the Python possession model being oracle validated, so the port has a correct reference to match rather than a moving target.
acceptance_criteria: Rust possession output is byte identical to Python parquet for the golden game fixtures and then for the full season. Divergences localize to a specific game and event via the differential harness.
notes: REAL GATE: the Python possession model must be oracle-validated before this starts. The dependency on the E5 research spike is a proxy; when that spike files its implementation issues, repoint this dependency at the one that produces validated possession parquet.

title: RESEARCH: Rust workspace, crate selection, differential test harness
description: Plan the port before starting it. Crate maturity is not a risk for the infrastructure layer - arrow at 77M downloads, parquet at 75M, polars 0.55 at 14.5M, duckdb, and axum at 464M are all well established. Note that polars is first class in Rust as well as Python, so the same library sits on both sides of the port and expression code maps closely between the two APIs, which makes the ingestion and feature layers substantially more mechanical to port. Decide the cargo workspace layout under rust/crates, the crate split, and how the differential test harness works: Python is the reference implementation, Rust must produce byte-identical parquet, and any divergence must localize to a specific game and event. Also confirm the build artifact budget from E1 holds, since a target dir with these dependencies is the largest single consumer of local disk.
acceptance_criteria: Workspace layout and crate split decided. Differential test harness designed, reusing the E7 comparison harness. Build artifact size measured against the local disk budget with debug symbols disabled. Port issues confirmed against the ordering already filed. Findings written to docs/research/ as a committed document. Target schema revised if the research warrants it. Implementation issues filed under this epic with dependencies set. This issue is NOT closed by writing code - it is closed by producing the findings and the issue breakdown.

title: RESEARCH: pin the gold/v1 contract and schema snapshot test
description: Reserve the API contract now without building the service. The failure this prevents is common and expensive: analysis marts evolve ad hoc, something starts consuming them, and they calcify into an accidental API with no version discipline. Decide the versioning scheme for gold marts, the rule that changes within a version must be additive only while breaking changes cut a new version directory, and implement a schema snapshot test that fails the build when a gold schema changes without a version bump. The eventual service is a thin read only axum layer over DuckDB with no business logic, so the pipeline language never constrains it - but that is later work, not this issue.
acceptance_criteria: Versioning scheme decided and documented. Schema snapshot test implemented and wired into the default test run. A deliberate decision recorded on what belongs in gold versus silver. No service code written. Findings written to docs/research/ as a committed document. Target schema revised if the research warrants it. Implementation issues filed under this epic with dependencies set. This issue is NOT closed by writing code - it is closed by producing the findings and the issue breakdown.

title: RESEARCH: triage analysis candidates into feasibility tiers
description: The rich model unlocks analyses grouped by the new axis each opens. SEQUENCE AND DEPENDENCY: possession transition matrices conditioned on previous possession end type - the original motivating question; momentum and hot-hand tested with lineup controls, which most published studies lack; an absorbing Markov chain over event states giving a poor-man's expected possession value without tracking data; and whether a run is statistically distinguishable from a random walk. FATIGUE AND REST, unlocked purely by lineup stints and genuinely underexplored: within-stint performance decay against consecutive seconds on court; rest differential as a possession covariate; coach rotation fingerprints. LINEUP STRUCTURE: synergy residual as lineup net rating minus sum of parts, giving player-pair chemistry. CONTEXT CONDITIONED EFFICIENCY: after-timeout efficiency by coach; transition versus half court splits; shot quality by shot clock bucket; the real value of an offensive rebound in points-per-possession terms. LEVERAGE: a possession level win probability model yielding a leverage index - the highest value single artifact, since it feeds clutch analysis, garbage time filtering and the flagship visualization at once. MATCHUPS from 2017: defender adjusted shot quality; cross-matching detection. OFFICIATING: foul rates by crew controlled for lineup and context. Triage these by feasibility and value, do not attempt all of them.
acceptance_criteria: Each candidate assigned a feasibility tier and a value assessment. A recommended ordering. Experiments filed as issues for the selected subset only. Candidates explicitly rejected are recorded with the reason, so they are not silently revisited. Findings written to docs/research/ as a committed document. Target schema revised if the research warrants it. Implementation issues filed under this epic with dependencies set. This issue is NOT closed by writing code - it is closed by producing the findings and the issue breakdown.

title: E10 Rust port (learning track)
description: Port the settled derivation core from Python to Rust, in an order chosen for teaching value. The pbpstats oracle is the port contract and both implementations are kept for differential testing, so correctness is externally defined at every step. The statistical layer stays in Python permanently.

title: E11 Read API
description: Deferred build, but the contract is reserved now: gold marts are versioned from the first mart and guarded by a schema snapshot test, so they cannot calcify into an accidental API. The eventual service is a thin read only axum layer over DuckDB.

title: E8 Analysis R&D
description: Novel analyses unlocked by the rich model. Triage candidates into feasibility tiers and run experiments. Covers sequence dependency, fatigue and rest, lineup chemistry, context conditioned efficiency, leverage, matchups, and officiating.

value: polars on Python 3.14: the 'polars' dist is a pure-Python shim; the compiled Rust lives in 'polars-runtime-32', which ships cp310-abi3 wheels. abi3 is forward-compatible with any CPython >= 3.10, and the tag names the MINIMUM version, never the actual one. So grepping published wheels for a cp314 (or cp313) tag finds nothing and falsely suggests polars does not support 3.14. Verified working: _polars_runtime.abi3.so, Tag cp310-abi3-macosx_11_0_arm64, on CPython 3.14.7. Caveat: polars' classifiers stop at 3.13, so this is verified-working rather than vendor-supported; fallback is python313. See docs/research/0001-polars-on-python-314.md
